pairs.old: Results after 5 years: Maryland hospitals generated $1.2B in Medicare savings, achieved lower per-capita cost growth than national trends, and showed quality improvements — particularly in preventable hospitalizations and readmissions.
pairs.new: Results after 5 years: the independent evaluation (RTI International, 2019) found $975 million in Medicare savings from 2014 to 2018 — total Medicare spending grew 2.8 percent more slowly than in a comparison group, with $796 million of the savings from hospital spending.
pairs.claim: fallback: 'Results after 5 years: Maryland hospitals generated $1.2B in Medicare savings ... quality improvements in preventable hospitalizations and readmissions'
pairs.src: RTI International final evaluation of the Maryland All-Payer Model (Nov 2019): $975M Medicare savings 2014-2018 (2.8% slower total spending growth), $796M from hospital spending

pairs.old: now runs in Maryland, Connecticut, Hawaii, Rhode Island and downstate New York;
